paper.title_en: Performance study of a glass RPC with low Global Warming Potential gas mixtures
paper.abstract_en: Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) are widely employed in high-energy physics experiments due to their excellent timing resolution and high detection efficiency. Conventional RPC operation relies on freon-based gas mixtures having high Global Warming Potential (GWP), contributing significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. In this work, the performance of a single-gap glass RPC detector (30 cm <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e257"><mo>×</mo></math> 30 cm) is studied using the standard gas mixture (C2H2F4 95%, i-C4H10 4.5%, SF6 0.5%) and eco-friendly alternatives based on CO2 and HFO gases. The detector was tested using cosmic muons, and its performance was evaluated in terms of efficiency, current–voltage characteristics, and timing resolution. The results show that eco-friendly gas mixtures achieve stable detector operation with high efficiency and only marginal degradation in timing performance, demonstrating their potential application to environmentally sustainable RPC operation.
